tasks.title: Add PerLinearFt RateType (prerequisite for pricing trim/wall-linear)
tasks.notes: RateType has no per-linear-foot. Add PerLinearFt='per_linear_ft' (+ label), wire LineItemFactory::unitFromRateType->'lf', seed a per-LF trim LaborRate. Must land before takeoff pricing. Files: app/Enums/RateType.php, LineItemFactory.php, LaborRateSeeder.php

prep.what: Add a PerLinearFt enum case to RateType, wire it through LineItemFactory, and seed one trim LaborRate using it — unlocking per-LF pricing for trim and wall-linear takeoff lines.
prep.understand: RateType drives how LineItemFactory computes unit costs. Today it has SF and EA variants but nothing for linear feet. Trim and wall-linear measurements from the blueprint seeder are measured in LF — without a PerLinearFt rate type, they price at $0 or default to the wrong unit. This is the smallest blocker in the chain: 30 minutes of enum + factory + seeder work that unlocks t48's pricing logic.
approach: Open `app/Enums/RateType.php` — add `PerLinearFt = 'per_linear_ft'` with a human label (e.g. 'Per Linear Foot').
In `LineItemFactory.php`, find `unitFromRateType` and add a case for `PerLinearFt` that returns `'lf'`.
In `LaborRateSeeder.php`, add at least one trim LaborRate row using the new PerLinearFt rate type with a realistic per-LF dollar amount.
Run `php artisan test` (or the relevant test subset) to verify nothing breaks; check the seeder runs clean with `php artisan db:seed --class=LaborRateSeeder`.
resources: `app/Enums/RateType.php` — the enum to extend
`app/Services/LineItemFactory.php` — find `unitFromRateType`, the switch to add the case to
`database/seeders/LaborRateSeeder.php` — add a trim rate row here
t48 notes — confirm which trades need LF pricing so the seeder covers them all

tasks.title: Derive wall PAINT area (perimeter x height) — the missing painting measurement
tasks.notes: A 2D plan has no wall height so painting gets ZERO auto-sqft today. Add a wall/ceiling height input (project default + optional per-room override); wall paint SF/room = perimeter x height (perimeter from geometry.rings / meta.perimeter; the seeder currently DROPS geometry — preserve it). Emit a 'Wall paint area' line per room. Add estimates.wall_height. Files: TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php, Takeoff Vue, migration

prep.what: Add a wall height field to takeoff projects (default + per-room override), preserve room perimeter from the blueprint geometry, and compute wall paint SF = perimeter x height — emitting a 'Wall paint area' line per room.
prep.understand: A 2D blueprint gives floor area and perimeter but no vertical dimension. Painting bids need wall SF = perimeter x height. Today `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php` silently DROPS the geometry (rings / meta.perimeter), so painting always gets zero area. Two things must happen: (1) stop dropping geometry — store the perimeter per room so the seeder can multiply it; (2) add a wall_height input on the project (a 9ft default covers most residential) with optional per-room override. The 'Wall paint area' line this emits feeds t46's trade routing and t48's pricing.
approach: Write a migration to add `wall_height` (decimal, nullable, default 9.0) to the `estimates` or `takeoff_projects` table (check which model owns project-level config).
In the Takeoff Vue component (`resources/js/Pages/Takeoff/Index.vue`), add a wall height input field (number, feet, default 9) plus an optional per-room height override in the room editor.
In `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php`, stop dropping geometry: preserve `geometry.rings` or `meta.perimeter` per room; compute `wall_paint_sf = perimeter * wall_height` for each room.
Emit a new `'Wall paint area'` line item per room in the seeded estimate output — use `kind = 'derived_wall_sf'` so t46 can route it to the painting trade.
Smoke-test: seed a takeoff for a sample blueprint and verify each room has a non-zero Wall paint area line with a plausible SF value.
resources: `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php` — the seeder that currently drops geometry; this is the main file
`resources/js/Pages/Takeoff/Index.vue` — Takeoff Vue component for the wall height input
Existing migrations in `database/migrations/` — find the one that created estimates or takeoff_projects to add the new column alongside
t46 notes — uses `kind = 'derived_wall_sf'` to route wall paint area to the painting trade

tasks.title: Route takeoff measurements to trades at the seam
tasks.notes: Every measurement collapses into one anonymous kind=custom $0 line, dropping kind+geometry (TakeoffEstimateSeeder). Preserve+switch on kind: area(SF)->flooring, derived wall SF->painting, line(LF)->wall-linear/trim, count(EA)->doors/tile. Tag each line with a trade via the core-vs-subbed helper. Rafa: 'quanto de tile, quanto de trim, quanto de tudo'. Files: TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php

prep.what: Fix TakeoffEstimateSeeder to route each measurement to the right trade by kind: area SF -> flooring, derived wall SF -> painting, line LF -> trim/wall-linear, count EA -> doors/tile — and tag each with a trade label.
prep.understand: Right now every blueprint measurement collapses into one anonymous `kind=custom` $0 line — all geometry and kind information is discarded. Rafa's ask is 'quanto de tile, quanto de trim, quanto de tudo' — a per-trade quantity breakdown. The fix is a routing switch on `kind` inside TakeoffEstimateSeeder, using the measurement kind to pick the right trade and rate. The 'core-vs-subbed helper' determines whether that trade is CT Pros crew vs subcontracted. This task assumes t45's derived_wall_sf line is already emitted.
approach: In `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php`, stop collapsing all measurements into `kind=custom`. Instead, switch on the measurement `kind` field: `area` -> flooring, `derived_wall_sf` (from t45) -> painting, `line` -> wall-linear/trim (use PerLinearFt from t47), `count` -> doors/tile.
For each routed line, call the core-vs-subbed helper (find it in `app/Services/` or `app/Helpers/`) to set the trade classification: whether CT Pros does it in-house or subs it out.
Verify geometry is not dropped — `kind` and quantity must flow through from the takeoff payload to the seeded estimate line.

Smoke-test: seed a takeoff project with rooms that have area + line + count measurements; verify the output has separate lines for flooring, painting (from t45), trim, and doors — each with a trade tag.
resources: `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php` — the only file touched in this task
The core-vs-subbed helper — search `app/Services/` for 'trade' or 'subbed' to find it
t45 output: `derived_wall_sf` kind — this is a new kind you'll need to handle in the switch
t47 output: `PerLinearFt` rate type — needed for the trim/wall-linear lines to have valid unit pricing

tasks.title: Price seeded takeoff lines by kind/trade -> LaborRate+MaterialTier (re-key t30)
tasks.notes: Key pricing on measurement kind+trade (area->flooring rate, derived-wall->painting rate, LF->per-LF trim), NOT fragile per-project classification strings (keep those as optional room labels). Depends on painting LaborRate rows + PerLinearFt. Corrects open task t30. Files: TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php

prep.what: Price each seeded takeoff line using its kind+trade to look up the right LaborRate row — replacing the brittle per-project string-matching pricing from t30.
prep.understand: After t46 routes measurements to trades, each line knows its kind (area/line/count/derived_wall_sf) and trade (flooring/painting/trim/doors). This task uses that to look up a `LaborRate` row and multiply: `quantity x LaborRate.unit_cost` + optional MaterialTier markup. The old pricing (t30) keyed on fragile room type strings that change or break. The new pricing keys on stable kind+trade enums. Depends on: painting LaborRate rows existing in the DB, and PerLinearFt (t47) so trim LF lines can price correctly.
approach: Read t30's notes to understand the original pricing intent — what model was designed but not yet cleanly implemented.

In `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php`, after trade routing (t46), for each line: look up `LaborRate WHERE trade = line.trade AND rate_type = matching_rate_type` (SF for area/paint, LF for trim, EA for count).
Set `line.unit_price = LaborRate.unit_cost` and `line.total = quantity * unit_price`; if a MaterialTier model exists, add the markup on top.
Add a guard for missing LaborRate rows: log a warning and set price to 0 rather than throwing — so a missing seeder row doesn't crash the whole takeoff seed.
Verify with a seed run: every routed line from t46 should now have a non-zero price (assuming t47's seeder added trim rates).
resources: `TakeoffEstimateSeeder.php` — pricing logic goes here, after the kind+trade routing from t46
t30 notes — original pricing spec this corrects; understand what the intent was
`LaborRate` model + `LaborRateSeeder.php` — the rate rows being looked up; t47 adds the PerLinearFt trim row
`MaterialTier` model (if it exists) — check `app/Models/` for it; add material markup if present

tasks.title: One-click 'Create estimate from this takeoff' from Review
tasks.notes: Today seeding needs an existing estimate + hand-typing takeoff_project_id into estimates/{id}/seed-from-takeoff. Add a button on the Review page/Takeoff Index row that creates a draft estimate + seeds it from the current takeoff project in one action, landing on estimate edit. Files: Takeoff Vue, EstimateController.php

prep.what: Add a 'Create Estimate' button to the Takeoff Review/Index page that atomically creates a draft estimate, seeds it from the current takeoff project, and redirects to the estimate edit page — replacing the current manual URL hack.
prep.understand: The current seeding flow requires: find an existing estimate ID, hand-type a URL (`estimates/{id}/seed-from-takeoff`), and manually enter the takeoff_project_id. That's a dead-end for real usage. The fix: one button -> one POST -> one redirect. The controller creates the draft estimate and triggers the seeder in a single action. This is the UX capstone that makes the entire blueprint takeoff feature usable without developer intervention.
approach: In `EstimateController.php`, add a `createFromTakeoff(TakeoffProject $takeoffProject)` action: wrap in a DB transaction — create a draft Estimate, call TakeoffEstimateSeeder with the new estimate ID, return the estimate.

Add the button to the Takeoff Index row or Review page (`resources/js/Pages/Takeoff/Index.vue`) — look for the existing row actions pattern (likely a dropdown or icon row) and add 'Create Estimate' that POSTs to the new route.
Register the route in `routes/web.php` (e.g. `POST /takeoff-projects/{takeoffProject}/create-estimate`).
On success, redirect to `estimates/{id}/edit` with a flash success message ('Draft estimate created and seeded from takeoff.').

Add a feature test: POST to the new endpoint with a valid takeoff project, assert a new Estimate row exists, assert the seeder was called (check for seeded line items), assert the redirect points to estimate edit.
resources: `EstimateController.php` — add the new `createFromTakeoff` action here
`resources/js/Pages/Takeoff/Index.vue` — find the row actions pattern; add the button
`routes/web.php` — register the new POST route

tasks.title: Definir direcao da integracao: pull (fiscal -> Despesas) vs push (Despesas -> Makro)
tasks.notes: Recomendacao: pull-first — RegEntradas/CadFornecedores/ControleFornecedores -> conciliar/preencher Despesas (read-only, menor risco, so depende de creds+CodEmpresa). Push (PcSalvaControleFornecedores) fica como fase posterior (exige escrita + IDs). Aguardando decisao do cliente/Haniel.

prep.what: Make the architectural decision for the Makro integration: pull (read NF/supplier data FROM Makro into GerenciaObra) or push (write despesas TO Makro) — then document it and break t47 into subtasks.
prep.understand: The MakroClient SOAP foundation is fully built (t42 done: envelope, auth header, parser, 8 tests green). The test base is live — you got a real 200 response from RegEstados. You've mapped 72 of Makro's WS consultas (docs/makro-consultas.md). Now you need to decide the integration DIRECTION before any business logic is built. Pull-first is the clear recommendation: use RegEntradas + CadFornecedores + ControleFornecedores to fetch fiscal entries and auto-fill/reconcile Despesas — read-only, no write permissions needed, unblocked as soon as Glaywson's production bank is activated. Push (PcSalvaControleFornecedores) is higher-risk and can be Phase 2.
approach: Open `docs/makro-consultas.md` and review the 72 mapped consultas — specifically look at RegEntradas (fiscal entries), CadFornecedores (supplier lookup), and ControleFornecedores (payables) to understand what pull data is available.
Review the existing MakroClient code (`app/Services/Makro/MakroClient.php`) and confirm `consulta()` already returns parsed array data ready for business logic.
Make the call: pull-first (recommended). Document the decision in a short ADR or note — which WS calls anchor the pull path, what fields map to Despesa fields.
Update the t47 task notes with the decided direction + break it into concrete subtasks (e.g. 'Build RegEntradas sync job', 'UI to show pending fiscal entries for reconciliation', etc.).
resources: `docs/makro-consultas.md` — the full 72-consulta API surface map from the sweep
`app/Services/Makro/MakroClient.php` — SOAP client with `consulta()` returning `array<int, array<string, string>>`
`scripts/makro-sweep.php` — the probe script; re-run against specific consultas if you need to verify a response shape
